Digitale Gesundheitslösungen verändern, wie Menschen versorgt werden – sicher, nutzerzentriert und evidenzbasiert. jobs.title: Technical Product Manager, Integrations
jobs.description:
Who we are
 Foundation models transformed text and images. Structured data - the largest and most consequential data format in the world - stayed untouched, until now. What LLMs did for language, we're doing for tables.
 We pioneered tabular foundation models: TabPFN v2 was a Nature cover story, has passed 3.5M+ downloads and 7,500+ GitHub stars, and runs in production from detecting lung disease with Oxford Cancer Analytics to preventing train failures with Hitachi . The hardest problems - millions of rows, real-time inference, entirely new modalities - are still open, and no one else is working on them at this level.
 We're a small, highly selective team of 40+ with backgrounds from Google, DeepMind, Meta, Apple, Amazon, Jane Street, and CERN, led by Frank Hutter , Noah Hollmann , and Sauraj Gambhir , and advised by Bernhard Schölkopf and Turing Award winner Yann LeCun.
 In July 2026, less than 18 months after our €9M pre-seed, we joined SAP as an independent frontier AI lab - same team, mission, and open-weights models, now backed by more than €1 billion over four years.
 
 The role 
 Most enterprises will never call our API directly. They will meet TabPFN inside the platforms they already run: SAP, AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Databricks, or their own cloud. How well that works, how fast each release arrives there, and which platforms come next is the job of our Technical Product Manager for Integrations.
 You take each model release from handover to live across every channel, working with the engineers who build the model and the partner teams who host it. Inside SAP you carry the product side of TabPFN across its platforms, from AI Core to SAP Analytics Cloud, and you help build the integration engineering team that will work with you. Several decisions are yours to bring to the table: which announced channels we build next, what a marketplace listing should cost, how support for all of this works.
 You work directly with our product team, our engineers and the founders, and you report to the CTO. This suits someone who enjoys landing things on a date as much as deciding what to build, and who still likes being close to the code.
 What you'll do 
 Take every model release live across SAP, the cloud marketplaces and customer environments, on a plan you build with product and engineering.

 Be the technical counterpart for the partner teams that host TabPFN, from SAP's platform teams to the hyperscaler marketplaces.

 Shape how TabPFN shows up inside SAP's stack and what the integration engineering team builds first.

 Bring the open channel decisions to the founders with a recommendation, and stay hands-on: listings, docs, smoke tests, a PR when it is faster than asking.

 What we're looking for 
 Two or more years as product manager for a platform or integration surface: a product that ships into partners' platforms, or that other companies build on.

 You have shipped through gates you did not control, landed multi-team releases on dates, and made a large enterprise's process work for a small, fast team.

 You started as an engineer and never fully stopped: you read code, logs and scan reports without a translator.

 You are in Berlin or ready to relocate; Freiburg or New York can work.

 What sets you apart 
 You have shipped into an SAP, Salesforce, Microsoft or Oracle ecosystem, or know the cloud marketplaces from the inside.

 You have deployed machine learning models and know what GPUs cost.

 You have worked at a startup, and you use AI tools to take real work off your plate.

 
 Life at Prior Labs
 You'll work alongside researchers and builders who hold themselves to a very high bar - in the quality of their work and in how they work with each other. We move fast and still take the time to do things right.
 Our teams are based in Berlin, Freiburg, and New York - when you're working on something as hard as TabPFN, being in the same room matters. But great people come from everywhere, and in exceptional cases we're open to remote, which usually means frequent travel to one of our offices. Wherever you're based, the whole company comes together regularly for offsites to build and celebrate together.
 
 Our Commitments
 The best products and teams are built by people with a wide range of perspectives and backgrounds. We welcome applications from all identities and walks of life - especially if you've ever felt discouraged by "not checking every box" - and provide equal opportunities regardless of gender, sexual orientation, origin, disability, or any other trait that makes you who you are.
 We care about how your data is handled - see our Recruiting Data Privacy page

jobs.title: Technical Product Manager
jobs.description:
Swarm Aero is redefining air power, building the largest swarming UAV and the most versatile swarming aircraft network in the world. The company is moving quickly to launch the first aircraft designed specifically for swarming, as well as the Command & Control software to mobilize swarms of thousands of heterogeneous autonomous assets and empower human operators to achieve superhuman results.
 The team has created and exited multiple startups, negotiated defense deals worth billions of dollars, and designed and built 30+ novel aircraft, with aerospace experience from Scaled Composites, Airbus, Archer Aviation, Blue Origin, and Boom Supersonic.
 
 Mission 
 Turn operational needs, customer feedback, and product direction into clear product specifications—and then drive those capabilities through decisions, design, development, and validation.
 You will work directly with the Head of Product on Legion and become a core contributor to both defining the product and running the process around it.
 
 What You’ll Own 
 Create clear, detailed product specifications for new features and capabilities.

 Take customer needs, operator feedback, technical constraints, and product direction and turn them into actionable product requirements.

 Own bounded features from early definition through design, development, feedback, and validation.

 Work directly with Product Design to translate specifications into detailed workflows and Figma designs.

 Review designs and implementations against product intent and requirements.

 Facilitate product discussions with government customers, third-party contractors, operators, engineers, and internal stakeholders.

 Prepare agendas and clearly identify topics requiring feedback, decisions, or alignment.

 Capture decisions, unresolved issues, customer feedback, and action items.

 Incorporate meeting outcomes directly into product specifications and related artifacts.

 Maintain feature status, decision history, feedback registers, and key product commitments.

 Identify ambiguity, conflicting requirements, and missing decisions before they slow the team down.

 Track important product and contractual deliverables.

 Help prepare product reviews, demonstrations, and customer discussions.

 Create enough structure to keep the organization aligned without introducing unnecessary process.
 

 What Great Looks Like 
 You are given a problem such as:
 “Operators need a better way to understand and respond to vehicle health issues during degraded communications.”
 You meet with the relevant operators, engineers, customers, and stakeholders.
 You understand the underlying problem.
 You separate customer requests from actual product requirements.
 You identify edge cases and unresolved decisions.
 You write a product specification that clearly explains the intended behavior, workflows, system states, requirements, and open questions.
 You work with Product Design to turn that specification into a strong interface.
 You incorporate feedback, resolve ambiguity, and keep the feature moving until the capability works as intended.
 The Head of Product provides direction and reviews the most important decisions—but does not need to personally produce every artifact or manage every follow-up.
 
 Early Expectations 
 Within the first few weeks, you should begin contributing directly to product specifications.
 Initially, you may draft sections of specifications or own smaller, well-bounded capabilities with guidance from the Head of Product.
 As your understanding of Legion, its operators, and the technical architecture grows, you will rapidly take ownership of larger features.
 We are not looking for someone who spends six months observing before contributing.
 
 The Person We’re Looking For 
 You are an excellent writer.
 You can take a complicated conversation and turn it into a clear product definition.
 You have strong product judgment and are comfortable making reasonable decisions when requirements are incomplete.
 You understand that a customer request is not automatically a product requirement.
 You are technically curious and capable of participating meaningfully in discussions with software engineers, systems engineers, operators, and external partners.
 You naturally ask questions like: 
 What problem are we actually trying to solve?

 Who needs this capability?

 What should happen in this edge case?

 What does the operator see?

 What state is the system actually in?

 How will we know this works?

 Is this a product decision, an engineering decision, or a customer preference?

 You are highly organized, but organization is a means to an end.

 Your real job is creating clarity and moving product decisions forward.

 
 Particularly Valuable Experience 
 Experience with any of the following would be especially valuable:
 Technical product management

 Complex B2B software

 Command-and-control systems

 Aerospace or defense

 Robotics or autonomous systems

 Mission planning

 Geospat

jobs.title: Junior Product Manager – IT Fulfillment
jobs.description:
Every order a Suitsupply customer places, online, in a store, or through customer service, has to be captured, understood and carried all the way through to delivery or return. As Junior Product Manager for IT Fulfillment, you will help build and improve the services that make that happen: the order flows, data and interfaces that connect our webstore, our stores, our warehouses and our customer service teams.
You will work in a small team inside the IT Fulfillment domain, alongside the Group Product Manager and our own engineers. The Group Product Manager shapes the functional direction with the business and sets priorities; together you turn it into clear requirements, well-defined tickets and working software, built with engineers and AI agents. This is a technical product role: we build our own services, so you will spend your time in data models, interfaces and requirements rather than managing a vendor’s roadmap. You start close to delivery, with support while you learn the domain, and grow into owning more of the roadmap.
What you will do
  • Turn mapped-out functional flows into clear, buildable work: technical requirements, acceptance criteria and user stories that engineers and AI agents can pick up without coming back with questions.
  • Own the detail as both product manager and business analyst: the data model, the way systems talk to each other, and the edge cases nobody thought of yet.
  • Break large changes into chunks that can be built, tested and released safely, and keep the backlog in a state where work can start at any moment.
  • Work with engineers day to day in refinement, planning, reviews and releases, and use our AI tooling to draft, structure and pressure-test the work before it reaches them.

jobs.title: Senior Product Design Manager, Enterprise
jobs.description:
About Scale AI

Scale AI accelerates the development and deployment of AI, from the high-quality training data and evaluation services that power the world's leading AI labs, to full-stack AI applications built for Enterprise, U.S. Public Sector, and Global Public Sector customers. We don't just hand over a model; we find the highest-value use case, build the system around it, and own the outcome, whether that's an agent supporting mission planning for the Department of Defense, a sovereign AI platform for a government ministry, or an agentic workflow inside a Fortune 500 enterprise. Our platform powers breakthroughs at the frontier of AI, and great design is how we make that power accessible, intuitive, and trusted by the teams who rely on it every day.

The Role

We're looking for a product design leader to lead and grow our enterprise team.

What You'll Do

  • Set the direction for Enterprise design. Define what exceptional design looks like for Scale's Applications customers making high-stakes decisions and for the expert contributors powering the platform. Translate the broader design vision into a clear, motivating direction for your team.
  • Build and lead the team. Own hiring, development, and day-to-day leadership for a growing team of designers. Create the culture and operating rhythms that let them do their best work.
  • Drive design execution across the Enterprise product. Partner with your Product and Engineering counterparts to set priorities and ensure design is involved from problem scoping through delivery, not brought in at the end.

 The Sunday Times Best Places to Work two years running

 In this role, you will join MoonPay’s Crypto Asset Management team as a Product Manager, helping us build and scale the liquidity and asset infrastructure that supports products across MoonPay.

 Your work will help the team move faster, improve the efficiency and resilience of our liquidity infrastructure, and enable MoonPay to support significantly more products and transaction volume as the business grows.

 This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys solving complex problems, wants to deepen their understanding of crypto and financial infrastructure, and is excited to develop their product craft in a fast-moving, high-impact environment.

 What You Will Do 

 
 
 Own day-to-day product execution across Crypto Asset Management initiatives, translating business, technical, operational, and compliance requirements into clear product requirements, user stories, project plans, and delivery milestones.

jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.description:
About Nous 
 Nous is a household AI agent. It takes over the bills and admin people don't have time for and acts for them: switching energy, buying insurance, cancelling forgotten subscriptions, managing the family calendar. Nearly 250,000 UK households have signed up, and another joins every minute.
 We think the real value of AI isn't writing amazing cover letters, it's doing useful things in the real world for real people. That's the hard part, and a brilliant product is only half of it. An energy switch takes weeks, so our agents run on long-running workflows, not a single chat turn. Cancelling a subscription means a browser agent handling the code Apple sends to your phone. Buying insurance meant getting our regulatory principal comfortable with an agent doing it end to end (a UK first), which comes down to knowing exactly when the LLM should hand over to rules because a mistake would cost someone real money.
 We're about 30 people running one agent across energy, broadband, mobile, insurance, mortgages and subscriptions (with more being added), each with its own suppliers, rules and ways of going wrong. With far more problems than people, a person or small team owns each one end to end, from spotting it in the data or a customer conversation to shipping the fix. And because the agent acts, you find out quickly whether the fix worked.
 Everyone builds here: a product engineer launched our subscription cancellation product within a couple of months of joining, and a PM rebuilt our WhatsApp agent.
 And it's working. We're growing more than 20x year on year, with a market-leading NPS above +80, and we manage well over half a billion pounds of household spending. We've raised more than $30M from Heartcore, Mosaic and a who's who of entrepreneurs who founded Monzo, GoCardless, lastminute.com and Onfido. But the real draw is the team - ask anyone here why they joined and you'll get some version of "to do great work with really smart people".
 The goal is household life that's simpler, cheaper and fairer, and most of that is still to build.
  
 How we build (worth reading before the role) 
 How products get built is changing fast. With AI tooling, a PM can prototype, dig into production data and commit production code to get a change live all in an afternoon. An engineer can own a product area end to end and decide what to build next.
 We're leaning into that. Our PMs lean into code and our engineers run products: one of our engineers owns the car insurance targets. We care about whatever gets the job done most effectively, regardless of once upon a time whose job it was meant to be.
 We're moving fast and adapting as we go, and we don't have all the answers yet. What should a squad look like when everyone can build? Where does process still help, and where does it just slow you down? What's a PM for when an engineer can run the experiment themselves? We're working it out, and we want someone who is excited to be part of helping figure it out.
  
 About the role 
 So where does a PM fit? A lot of our work still suits squads: clear targets, a few service lines and a team of engineers. Those squads need product managers to run them. All our roles in product overlap, but this one is centred on product management. If you’d rather spend all your time building, have a look at our Product Builder role.
 You’ll take a squad responsible for a key section of our product and service lines and grow them: expand what they cover, understand the levers that drive their performance (automation, new suppliers, what we recommend to members) and increase their commercial value.
 Being a Product Manager at Nous is one of the hardest roles we have. The product is complex and we move fast, so you need to be able to hold a lot of context. You'll switch between very different things all day: thinking about OKRs and the plan for the next couple of weeks one moment, getting a PR into production the next, while helping unblock an engineer.
 That's also what makes it exciting.
 You bring order to fast-moving work, get some sequencing in place so people aren’t each figuring it out on their own, evaluate what’s being shipped, own the reporting and keep the squad’s energy up. You won’t hesitate to make changes yourself, but you won’t be just another builder in the squad either: when you’re heads-down building, you can’t unblock anyone or bring the team together.
 Growing a service line here means working across the boundary between product and commercial, so we’re particularly interested in PMs who’ve had real exposure to the commercial side of a business.
 Our agent acts in the real world a lot, so saving someone money takes more than great product execution. We also need access to the best tariffs and suppliers, and we have to understand the regulation we operate in. And because Nous is an agent, your nice neat Amplitude funnels don't work: every user's journey can be totally different. So we're after PMs who are excited by everything it

Company Description 
 We’re Checkout.com . You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day. 
 
 We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers. 

 Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale. 

 If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact. 

 With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started. 
 
 Join us at ProcessOut
 ProcessOut is a pioneer in the payment orchestration space. We are on a mission to help merchants build, scale and optimize their payment infrastructure. We work to bring simplicity, flexibility & performance to payments.
 Millions of transactions are routed via ProcessOut everyday for merchants all over the world. We are proud to partner with amazing merchants like Glovo, Bolt, Sainsbury’s, Dott, Hellofresh and many more!
 We were acquired by Checkout.com in 2020 with the goal of growing our global reach.
 If you are looking to join a very fast-moving company with passionate, hard-working & fun teams, ProcessOut is for you! At ProcessOut, we are looking for people who are convinced they can play a central part in the Company's success! We are looking for people who are passionate, who are looking to achieve their full potential & who will actively contribute to strengthen the links between our teams. We value people that fully own their work and are passionate about building the next generation of online payments with us.
 
 Project Management at ProcessOut 
 As a Mid-level Project Manager within our Integrations Team, you will sit at the heart of our merchants expansion. The team is dedicated to:
 Architecting payments framework that guarantee high velocity and uncompromising quality for new payment providers on-boarding.

 Integrating with a global network of payment providers.

 In this high-impact role, your key responsibilities will include:
 Own the planification of a team of 10+ engineers, which will involve collecting the needs from merchants

 Orchestrating complex merchant timelines and delivery projects, championing excellence at every stage.

 Cultivating and maintaining strategic partnerships with global payment providers (we have more than 100, but only few are strategical)

 We operate as a self-sufficient, fully agile unit. To thrive here, you should:
 Possess a deep understanding of both payment ecosystems and engineering principles.
 You'll collaborate with Europe's leading merchants, work alongside world-class engineers and discuss with banks from all around the world

 
 Masterfully navigate complex trade-offs and rapid context switching in a dynamic environment.

 Drive external communication and engage directly, with often physical visits, with partners across Europe.

 Being able to challenge other remits (engineering, product, merchants, providers) with data driven decisions

 We are experiencing constant growth in the number of transactions handled, new clients, and integrations. That’s why we pay very close attention to efficiency and we are happy to improve our processes.
 
 About you 
 At least 5 years of experience in payments

 Know your way around web-related tech (HTTP, TLS, proxies, API conventions...)

 Have a technical background and is able to understand software code

 Able to communicate with third-party providers from both a technical perspective and business

 Be product minded

 Always curious and passionate about understanding the business

 Nice to have 
 French language

 Cards payments knowledge

 What you will be doing 
 Working with engineers, merchants and payments providers to connect ProcessOut to worldwide acquirers and payment methods

 Contributing to the business by computing KPIs and improving our processes in order to improve them

 Own the product vision to help on designing, building, and releasing new features

 If you don't meet all the requirements but think you might still be right for the role, please apply anyway. We're always keen to speak to people who connect with our mission and values.
 
 Additional Information 
 Bring all of you to work 
 We create the conditions for high performers to thrive, through real ownership, fewer blockers, and work that makes a difference from day one.
 Here, you’ll move fast, take on meaningful challenges, and be recognized for the impact you deliver. It’s a place where ambition gets met with opportunity, and where your growth is in your hands.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager II, Consumer (all genders)
jobs.description:
The role

HelloFresh serves millions of customers weekly across 18 business units and 8 brands worldwide. At the heart of our product is a belief that every customer deserves a menu that feels like it was made for them, the right meals, at the right time, for the right person. We call it the Sous Chef vision.

As Senior PM II on the Personalization Experience team, you own what makes that vision real and felt. You're not building the ranking algorithm, you're building the experiences that make customers trust it, the data collection that makes it smart, and the moments where someone thinks: this app actually knows me.

This is a high-autonomy role at the intersection of consumer UX, engineering, and ML systems. The problems are genuinely hard, the scale is real, and the decisions are yours to make.

What you’ll do

  • Food Profile Quality & Signal Collection: The food profile is the raw material that powers everything downstream. Your job is to move customers from "fields filled in" to truly Personalization-Ready: high-signal, validated, actionable. You'll own and iterate on the collection experiences that give our models the data they need to perform.
  • The "Sous Chef" Feel & Transparency: You build the moments where personalization becomes tangible, the places where we tell customers why certain meals were chosen for them. This isn't just UX work, it's trust infrastructure for the entire personalization stack.
  • Cross-Org Data Supplier: You're the clean, reliable interface between raw signal and downstream experience, owning the explanation payloads and API contracts that make it all work at scale. You operate across organizational boundaries and align on shared metrics without needing to own the surfaces.
  • AI-Native Discovery You use GenAI tools actively to compress discovery-to-decision cycles, synthesizing global customer signals, stress-testing hypotheses, and arriving at decision-ready specs faster than traditional PM workflows allow. You don't treat AI as a novelty; it's a genuine speed and quality multiplier in your daily practice.
  • Long-Horizon Strategy You manage your domain with real autonomy. You run a flywheel: better profile data → better models → more visible personalization → more signal back to personalization. You own the strategy and sequencing, not just the backlog, thinking 12–18 months out and making the calls that shape the direction of the team.

What you’ll bring

  • Deep personalization or data-collection PM experience. 5+ years of PM experience, with meaningful time on user-facing personalization or data collection products, ideally where the UX is the data pipeline, and where you've shipped for both end customers and downstream data consumers.
  • Strong product taste and customer-facing craft. You have a genuine feel for what makes a consumer experience compelling, trustworthy, and sticky, not just functional. You've built products at scale where millions of people interact with what you ship, and you hold a high bar for the details: the copy, the interaction pattern, the moment of delight. You know the difference between a feature that works and one that earns trust.
  • Data-native. You query your own data (SQL/Python), define your own input/output KPIs, and hold your own in deep-dive technical discussions without needing a data analyst to translate.
  • Cross-org credibility. You've shipped products across organizational boundaries, aligning on shared metrics, maintaining clean contracts with engineering partners, and navigating competing priorities without direct authority.
  • Experimentation with healthy skepticism. You design experiments to validate hypotheses and know how to interpret results without over-indexing on noise. You've made hard calls to kill features based on data.
  • Exceptional communicator. You can make a complex algorithmic concept legible to a non-technical VP and you can write a spec that engineers can actually ship from.
  • The AI edge. You've already incorporated AI-assisted workflows into your daily practice to increase speed, depth of insight, and output quality.

What we offer

Elevate your lifestyle! Join one of Europe's fastest-growing tech powerhouses in a dynamic phase of expansion.

  • Immerse yourself in a diverse global community of 90+ nationalities.
  • Enjoy a competitive compensation package that goes beyond the norm, with perks like a HelloFresh- subsidized Pension Scheme, Berlin relocation support, and a Hybrid working model.
  • Elevate y

jobs.description:
Health can’t wait . 
 Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t.
 Alan exists to end the wait.
 Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way.
 So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience.
 We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture . We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR.
 Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond.
 ⭐ The Product Marketing Manager B2C opportunity
 Building the engagement engine with Alan Play that makes 500k members come back to their health every single day, a key differentiator for Alan. 
  
 Today, 25k Alan members open Alan Play every day (120,000 every month) to walk, meditate, breathe, compete with their colleagues, build healthy habits. Play is Alan's #1 source of traffic and the retention engine of all our health services. And we are B2B2C: companies pay, members choose to engage. Play is a differentiator in deals, and at renewal. HR admins are also an underused distribution channel to reach members. Two audiences, one product story. By 2030 we want 500k daily users, across all our countries
  
 The challenges: Our lifecycle is greenfield. Onboarding, activation, reminders, reactivation and win-back are owned by nobody today. We run events rebuilt almost from scratch, so the tenth Alan Cup costs as much as the first. We measure opens and clicks, not what a campaign actually did to daily engagement. And on the B2B side, our pitch goes stale between releases, as Play ships fast, so the sales argument does not keep up.
  
 The future: A lifecycle layer designed for personalisation, running on the segmentation and experimentation platform Play has been building. Campaign machinery that gets cheaper every quarter. A measurement loop we trust, with holdouts and real incrementality. A live Play pitch that updates as features ship, so the field walks into a renewal or a deal with the current product. And HR admins turned into a real, measured distribution channel rather than a mailing list.
  
 The hard parts: This role is horizontal, and vertical. Many member segments, many admin segments, several countries, coordination with Product as well as Sales, KAM and CSM, as well as other products teams who communicate with members.

Join us in this exciting journey, where your contributions will directly impact how businesses connect with their customers in a rapidly evolving global market.

Our team of passionate and innovative engineers, designers, and product managers architect tools that empower businesses to thrive in the evolving digital landscape, streamlining digital ordering for delivery and on-premise services . jobs.title: Product Manager, Editing Foundations
jobs.description:
About us 
 Founded in 2019 and part of Y Combinator's 2020 cohort, Photoroom is the leading visual solution for e-commerce.

We've raised Series B funding and reached 300+ million users worldwide, processing over 5 billion images annually and serving both small businesses and major enterprises like Amazon, DoorDash, and Decathlon through our mobile app, web platform, and API.

We're a team of 100+ passionate builders giving e-commerce businesses superpowers to create visuals that help them grow, making the hardest parts of selling online disappear. We focus on craft, innovation, and collaboration to create exceptional impact for e-commerce businesses worldwide.

 Role Summary
 We're looking for a Product Manager to own the editor: the surface every Photoroom user touches, on iOS, Android and the web. You'll sit in our Product Foundations team, whose mission is to build the core experiences that power Photoroom. You will work on the last-mile editing problem, giving users control with fine-grained edits for photos and videos. Working closely with engineers, designers, and the PMs who depend on you, you'll decide what gets built, why, and how it ships.
 Location: Paris, Ile de France (Hybrid) 

 About the role
 Own the single- and multi-image editing experiences end to end. Build one unified visual editing experience across three platforms, iOS, Android, Web and API.

 Integrate visual editing experiences within chat editing. Photoroom gives users the ability to start with AI generation and then graduate into fine-grained editing tasks. You’ll work hand-in-hand with our researchers and engineers to make sure our users can traverse the full editing journey in Photoroom.

 Define the problem before the solution. Sharpen the user problem, then partner with design and engineering to ship work that feels effortless. On a surface this heavily used, the difference between "works" and "feels right" is the whole job.

 Stay close to the user. Talk to e-commerce sellers every week, watch them edit, and feed what you hear directly into roadmap decisions.

 Use data to decide, not to justify. Pull and interpret data yourself, including crash rates, latency and cross-platform parity, to form hypotheses, measure what shipped, and call what's next. You won't need to wait around for someone else to run the query.

 About You
 You've shipped products people love. Five+ years as a PM, with multiple launches where you’ve convincingly solved the user problem and delivered business value.

 You've owned a creative product surface. An editor, a canvas or another tool where you are giving a user creative control.

 AI has reshaped how you work. You use Claude or equivalent every day, for prototyping, testing with users, or automating the parts of the job that used to fill your calendar. The value you bring sits in strategy and direction, not in writing tickets.

 You have demonstrable product taste. You can show specific work where the details matter and explain the calls you made, including the ones you'd make differently now. Craft in an editor is measured in milliseconds and pixels.

 You create clarity from ambiguity. Given a fuzzy problem, you take action rather than waiting for direction: you structure it, decide what matters, and move.

 You're data-fluent. You pull, interpret, and challenge data yourself, and use it to form a point of view rather than confirm one.

 You thrive in small teams with high autonomy. You can ship without being managed, and can operate in a fully remote, async-first environment that offers no scaffolding around you.

 Nice to have: experience building creative tools or any product where craft and visual quality matter; an understanding of photography or videography; experience shipping native mobile alongside web; entrepreneurial experience (you've started, built, or run something).
 
 Benefits
 30 days annual leave plus local public holidays

 Competitive equity package with stock options/BSPCE, giving you ownership in our growing company

 €1000 one-time home office grant OR €400 per month co-working space stipend

 €1,000 annual learning and development budget for training, courses, books, and skill development

 Private health insurance

 Access to personalised mental health support, including 1:1 sessions with therapists or coaches, self-care tools, and well-being resources via MokaCare

 Sports and cultural activities reimbursement

 Relocation support (up to 10k) available for those choosing to move to France, including apartment finding and visa assistance

 Note: Visa sponsorship and relocation support are only available for positions based in France. We cannot sponsor visas for remote positions outside of France.

 Culture fit interviews and meet the team (~3h in total)

jobs.title: Product Manager
jobs.description:
About Lio
 Build AI that runs inside the world's largest enterprises. 
 Everyone is building AI. Very few are making it work at enterprise scale.
 At Lio, we're building the AI workforce for procurement. Our AI agents automate complex, mission-critical workflows across procurement, logistics, and finance for some of the world's largest companies.
 Backed by leading investors including a16z and Y Combinator, we're growing fast and tackling some of the most complex challenges in enterprise AI.
 We're looking for people who want to take ownership, solve hard problems, and build technology that delivers real business impact.
 
 The Role
 We're looking for a Product Manager – Pre-Sales & Go-to-Market who can bridge the gap between what enterprise customers need, what our engineers build, and how we bring our products to market.
 At Lio, product decisions don't happen in isolation. Every customer conversation, sales cycle, and implementation reveals new opportunities to make our AI agents more valuable.
 Your mission is to turn those insights into action.
 You'll work directly with our Sales, Engineering, Marketing, and Implementation teams to understand customer needs, shape product positioning, strengthen our go-to-market strategy, and identify opportunities that drive revenue.
 You'll be deeply involved in enterprise sales cycles, helping our teams communicate the value of our AI agents, build compelling business cases, and win customers.
 This isn't traditional Product Management. 
 Our engineers own their features and make most product decisions. You won't manage a backlog or spend your time writing detailed specifications.
 Instead, you'll provide the customer context, commercial insights, and clear recommendations that help our engineers build the right things and our Sales team sell them effectively.
 We care about real customer value and commercial outcomes, not features that look impressive but never get used.
 
 What You'll Do
 Connect product and go-to-market: Work across Sales, Engineering, Marketing, and Implementation to align customer needs, product capabilities, and commercial opportunities.

 Get close to customers: Participate in enterprise discovery calls, demos, workshops, and sales conversations to understand buying criteria, pain points, and emerging use cases.

 Enable our Sales team: Develop compelling product messaging, use-case positioning, business cases, and sales materials that translate technical capabilities into measurable business value.

 Turn market insights into product improvements: Collect customer feedback, analyze win/loss patterns, and identify recurring opportunities for new or improved AI agents.

 Influence product decisions: Work directly with engineers to clarify customer problems, validate opportunities, and recommend priorities based on commercial potential and customer impact.

 Own product knowledge: Build and maintain the product and go-to-market knowledge base used by our teams and internal AI systems, ensuring capabilities, use cases, and proof points stay accurate.

 Analyze commercial performance: Understand how our products perform across customer segments, sales cycles, usage, and revenue.

 Improve pricing and packaging: Identify opportunities to strengthen our commercial offering, increase conversion, and unlock expansion.

 Understand the market: Stay close to competitors, industry developments, and emerging customer requirements.

 What We're Looking For
 2+ years of experience in Product Management, Solutions Consulting, Pre-Sales, or a comparable customer-facing role.

 Experience in B2B SaaS, ideally within a fast-growing startup or scale-up selling to enterprise customers.

 Direct involvement in enterprise sales cycles, including discovery, demos, business cases, and commercial discussions.

 Strong technical understanding and experience working closely with engineering teams.

 Familiarity with AI and LLM-based products and the ability to translate technical capabilities into business value.

 Strong commercial judgment and an understanding of what drives customer adoption, conversion, and revenue.

 Analytical skills and the ability to turn customer feedback, market signals, and performance data into clear recommendations.

 Excellent communication skills in English; German is a plus.

 A proactive, hands-on mindset with high ownership and the confidence to challenge assumptions.

 Experience using AI tools in your daily work.

 Procurement experience is a plus, but not required. We're looking for someone who can quickly understand a complex market and connect customer needs with real business opportunities.

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Cruise Liners & Port Operations
jobs.description:
At Kpler, we are dedicated to helping our clients navigate complex markets with ease. By simplifying global trade information and providing valuable insights, we empower organisations to make informed decisions in commodities, energy, and maritime sectors. 

 

 Since our founding in 2014, we have focused on delivering top-tier intelligence through user-friendly platforms. Our team of over 850 experts from 69 countries works tirelessly to transform intricate data into actionable strategies, ensuring our clients stay ahead in a dynamic market landscape. Join us to leverage cutting-edge innovation for impactful results and experience unparalleled support on your journey to success. 

 
 

 Kpler is expanding into high-value maritime verticals, with Cruise Liners and Port Operations representing two important opportunities. Both address a common market need: the lack of independent, reliable insights into actual performance, built on observed data rather than published schedules or self-reported information.

 In the cruise sector, operators and analysts often rely on published itineraries rather than actual vessel movements, despite the significant fuel and carbon costs associated with fleet operations. In ports, performance data is often incomplete or self-reported, creating a need for independent benchmarking as berth-level emissions carry increasing financial implications under schemes such as the EU ETS.

 As a Senior Product Manager, Cruise Liners & Port Operations, you will own both products end to end, from strategy and roadmap through to the first release and go-to-market. Working closely with the Lead Product Manager – Maritime & Logistics, you will build two early-stage products in parallel, leveraging Kpler’s network of more than 13,000 AIS receivers and over 10,000 mapped ports and berths.

 For Cruise Liners, you will develop itinerary intelligence for tracked fleets, providing an independent view of actual sailed itineraries, fuel consumption and emissions. For Port Operations, you will build a product focused on port-level vessel activity monitoring, giving port authorities a reliable, live view of activity and performance.

 This is an individual-contributor role for an experienced product professional with a background in maritime, cruise, travel, ports or an adjacent B2B data/SaaS environment. You will need to balance competing priorities across two products, establish trusted data methodologies, engage customers and bring both products to market through a pragmatic, build-and-iterate approach.

 

 Key Responsibilities 
 

 Own the product strategy and roadmap for Cruise Liners and Port Operations, prioritising customer needs and commercial opportunities while making trade-offs between the two products explicit.

 Lead market discovery with cruise operators, port authorities, harbour masters and terminal operators, gathering requirements and translating customer needs into product priorities.

 Drive delivery across both products, maintaining clear roadmaps, delivery cadences and launch plans, with a pragmatic approach focused on launching initial capabilities and iterating based on feedback.

 Establish trusted data and benchmarking methodologies for both products, developing an independent view of cruise itineraries, fuel and emissions, alongside consistent port call-cycle measurement and performance benchmarking.

 Collaborate with Engineering, Data, Sales, Product Marketing and other product teams to align delivery, reuse shared data and emissions capabilities, and develop early data and distribution partnerships.

 Define the Cruise Liners product direction, delivering fleet itinerary intelligence based on live, observed vessel movements that reflects actual sailed journeys rather than published schedules.

 Build the Port Operations product, providing port authorities with a reliable, live view of vessel activity using Kpler’s AIS receiver network and mapped port and berth data.

 Develop product positioning and competitive strategy, identifying opportunities to differentiate Kpler’s independent, first-party observed data from existing cruise analytics and port operations offerings.

 Drive go-to-market execution for both products, working with Product Marketing on positioning, packaging, pricing input and launch planning, and establishing repeatable customer discovery and design partnerships.

 6–10 years of senior product or commercial experience in maritime data, cruise or travel, ports, or an adjacent B2B data/SaaS business, with a proven track record of delivering products that customers adopt.

 Working fluency in at least one of cruise or port operations, with the ability to develop expertise quickly in the other.

 Direct experience in the cruise or ports industry, with an established network among operators, port authorities and terminals.

 Experience translating customer needs into product strategy and working closely with product and engineering team

jobs.title: AI Project Manager
jobs.description:
ParetoLabs is looking for an experienced and structured (Senior) AI Project Manager to lead AI projects for our clients from first idea to production.
 As part of our dynamic team, you will be the link between our clients, our engineers and the AI technologies we build with. You will scope projects, steer delivery and make sure what we ship creates real value in Swiss companies across a wide range of industries.
 About ParetoLabs 
 ParetoLabs is a Zurich-based software studio that develops customized, AI-powered applications for conversational and text-processing use cases. We help companies quickly test, implement, and scale AI applications within their specific business environments.
 Founded in 2023, ParetoLabs is a Microsoft for Startups partner that combines innovative AI technologies with the individual requirements of Swiss companies.
 Tasks
 Lead AI projects end to end — retrieval assistants, copilots and agents — from discovery and scoping to rollout and operation.
 Translate business problems into clear use cases, requirements and success criteria together with our clients.
 Plan and steer delivery with our engineering team: scope, timeline, budget, risks and priorities.
 Define how quality is measured and make sure solutions are evaluated before and after go-live.
 Work with client stakeholders on data, security, compliance and change management.
 Collaborate closely with our multicultural team and bring your own ideas to projects with real-world impact.
 Requirements
 Experience: Several years of project management in software, data or digital transformation projects; AI or data projects are a strong plus.
 AI Understanding: A solid grasp of how large language models, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and AI agents work, what they are good at and where they fail.
 Technical Foundation: Enough understanding of software architecture and cloud infrastructure (ideally Microsoft Azure) to discuss solutions with engineers and client IT and security teams.
 Methods: Confident with agile delivery and with structuring ambiguous problems into concrete plans.
 Stakeholder Management: Experience working with business and IT stakeholders up to management level, including managing expectations about what AI can and cannot do.
 Data & Compliance: Awareness of data protection (Swiss FADP, GDPR) and information security in client projects.
 Communication Skills: Excellent German and English, written and spoken.
 Mindset: Structured, hands-on and curious, with the ownership to bring projects over the finish line.
 Benefits
 Competitive Remuneration: A competitive salary package, reflecting your experience and contributions.
 Pick Your Gear: Choose your preferred devices for work.
 Attractive Benefits: above market pension benefits and a private accident insurance.
 Professional Growth: Participation in the Microsoft for Startups program, offering access to valuable resources, events and support.
 Interested in leading AI projects that make a real difference? We would be happy to hear from you.
 Please send us your CV and, if available, examples of projects you have led.
 Join ParetoLabs and shape how Swiss companies put AI to work!

jobs.title: Staff Product Manager: Product Discovery Engine
jobs.description:
Staff Product Manager, Product Discovery Engine 
 
 About Us 
 Constructor powers product search and discovery for some of the largest retailers in the world. We serve billions of requests every week, and you’ve probably seen our results somewhere and used our product without knowing it. We differentiate ourselves by focusing on metrics over features, and reinventing search and discovery from the ground up as a machine learning challenge with the specific goal of improving metrics like revenue. We’re approximately doubling year over year despite the market slowing down and have customers in every eCommerce vertical. We’re a passionate team of technologists who love solving problems and want to make our customers’ and coworkers’ lives better. We value empathy, openness, curiosity, continuous improvement, and are excited by metrics that matter. We believe that empowering everyone in a company to do what they think is best can lead to great things.
 
 Job Summary 
 We’re looking for a systems-minded Staff Product Manager to take Constructor’s search and discovery to the state of the art — and keep it there — across every retail industry we serve. This is a highly technical, high-leverage role at the core of our Product Discovery Engine chapter: the teams responsible for how we retrieve, understand, and rank the right products for every shopper, on every query, for every customer.
 Your job is to raise discovery quality and, through it, our customers’ business metrics. You won’t be measured on features shipped — you’ll be measured on relevance and business outcomes, like conversion, revenue per visit, and search-attributed GMV, moving up.
 You’ll start embedded with our Search Quality team, owning its strategy and roadmap and getting deep into the systems that decide what shoppers actually see. Over time, your mandate grows to setting direction for the entire Product Discovery Engine chapter — deciding where we’re heading and why across recall, ranking, query understanding, personalization, and the ML infrastructure underneath. This is a Staff role today with a clear path to Director as you take on chapter-wide leadership.
 Search at Constructor is fundamentally a machine learning problem, so this role lives and breathes ML. You’ll partner closely with ML, data science, and engineering to turn the latest research into production wins, keep us ahead of both commercial competitors and academic state of the art, and be the connective tissue that aligns multiple teams — ML Recall, ML Infra, and, over time, teams like CORE, SABR, and Catalog Management — behind a single, coherent vision for great discovery.
 If you’re excited about driving innovation across dozens of the world’s largest retailers, being held to relevance and business outcomes, and pushing an already best-in-class product further ahead, this role is for you.
 
 What You’ll Do 
 Own business impact, not features. Drive measurable lift in search-attributed conversion, revenue per visit, and GMV alongside relevance across our customer base.

 Deliver across every retail industry. Move quality and business metrics across all the verticals we serve, accounting for the differences in catalog, language, and shopper intent.

 Keep us at the state of the art. Continuously translate the latest ML / IR research and competitive moves into production wins, and ship SOTA ML / LLM-assisted capabilities that beat our previous best on relevance.

 Set chapter vision and strategy. Define the multi-quarter direction for the Product Discovery Engine — where we’re heading and why — tie it directly to customer business outcomes, and rally teams behind it.

 Lead Search Quality first. Own its strategy and roadmap, driving measurable improvements in the relevance and correctness of results.

 Orchestrate across the pipeline. Unify recall, ranking, query understanding, and personalization behind one definition of quality and one set of business metrics, so improvements compound instead of colliding.

 Turn ML research into production wins. Partner deeply with ML and data science to take models — from candidate generation and recall to LLM-assisted interpretation — from idea to production, balancing accuracy, latency, and cost.

 Make quality measurable and explainable. Build the metrics, evaluation frameworks, and tooling the whole chapter uses to measure, attribute, and explain discovery quality and its business impact.

 Own quality under pressure. Lead investigation and triage when issues arise, and design durable, systemic fixes rather than one-off patches.

 Grow the mandate. Expand into chapter-wide leadership spanning ML Recall, ML Infra, and — over time — teams like CORE, SABR, and Catalog Management.

jobs.title: Project Manager - Avionics, GNC & Flight Software
jobs.description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecrafts for humanity.
 The Avionics, Guidance, Navigation and Control (GNC), and Flight Software (FSW) functions are central to the safe and reliable operation of the vehicle. Together, they provide the electronic systems, control capabilities and software that guide Nyx through its mission - from launch and on-orbit operations to docking, re-entry and recovery.
 We are looking for a motivated and experienced Project Manager — Avionics, GNC & Flight Software to coordinate the development and delivery of these critical domains within the Nyx program.
 
 Your Mission
 As Project Manager for Avionics, GNC and Flight Software, you will be responsible for coordinating the execution of these work packages and ensuring that their development remains aligned with the overall Nyx program objectives.
 You will work closely with Avionics, GNC and FSW technical leads, systems engineering, propulsion, mission operations, verification and integration teams. Your role will be to create transparency on scope, schedule, interfaces, risks and decisions, while supporting the teams in delivering robust and well-verified capabilities for the vehicle.

 Ensure that technical, program and interface dependencies between Avionics, GNC, FSW, systems engineering, propulsion and mission operations are identified and actively managed.

 Support the planning and execution of avionics integration, software and hardware-in-the-loop activities, simulations, system integration and mission rehearsals.

 Coordinate inputs to design reviews, development reviews, qualification activities and other program milestones.

 Track the preparation and closure of requirements, verification activities, test results, documentation and technical actions.

 Identify schedule and delivery risks early, define mitigation actions with the relevant owners and escalate unresolved issues when required.

 Support the management of changes to scope, requirements, interfaces and priorities, ensuring that their impacts are understood.

 Prepare clear progress updates, decision material and status reports for program and project reviews.

 Facilitate regular coordination meetings and ensure that actions, decisions and commitments are recorded and followed through.

 Contribute to resource and capacity planning for the GNC and FSW activities.

 Support coordination with external partners, suppliers and customers when relevant to the project scope.

 Contribute to the continuous improvement of project-management processes, planning practices and reporting routines within the Nyx program.

 Practical experience managing plans, milestones, dependencies, risks, actions and technical deliverables.

 The ability to understand technical topics sufficiently to ask the right questions, identify impacts and support informed decisions.

 Experience working across requirements, design, implementation, integration, testing and verification activities.

 Strong organizational and communication skills, with the ability to bring structure and transparency to complex projects.

 A proactive approach to identifying risks, raising issues early and driving actions to closure.

 The ability to work effectively with technical experts while maintaining focus on program objectives and delivery commitments.

jobs.title: Product Management Director – Soft FM & Estates (UK)
jobs.description:
About SINGU 
 
 At SINGU , we’re redefining how the world’s most ambitious real estate companies run their operations. Our mission is to become Europe’s leading platform for managing warehouse, logistics, retail, and multi-site commercial real estate portfolios — empowering our Clients to protect revenue, boost efficiency, and unlock new value across every aspect of their business.
  
 Our unified CAFM platform already powers the daily operations of over 250 million m² of real estate worldwide , supporting more than 500,000 professionals. Following our union with the UK’s Micad and Germany’s net-haus, we now help manage 100,000+ buildings across 35+ countries — and we’re just getting started.
  
 Backed by a leading growth equity investor, we’re scaling rapidly and partnering with global leaders such as Prologis, ECE, CTP, Hillwood, Logicor, GLP, and Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield. As we continue to grow through strategic acquisitions and bold innovation, we stay true to our core values: adaptability, collaboration, and client focus. 
  
 If you’re ready to help build Europe’s leading platform for property operations — and make a tangible impact on how the real estate industry works — join SINGU and be part of this transformation. 
 
 About the Role 
 
 You'll own a significant slice of the SINGU product suite: space management and Soft FM services – cleaning standards, portering, and catering – used every day primarily across the UK healthcare market . Product-market fit is established and thousands of users depend on these products daily. What the portfolio needs now is strategic direction and taking them to their next level of growth.
 You'll do that through a team of four Product Managers who are domain experts in the products they run. This is a hands-on leadership role . You'll stay close to customer problems yourself, you'll raise the bar on how the team discovers and validates work, and you'll have real autonomy to decide what's worth building – and to prove it works.
 SINGU group grows both organically and through acquisition, and several of these products arrived with the companies that built them. You'll shape the strategy for bringing them into one coherent ecosystem and lead your team through that change. If you enjoy taking a set of good but separate products and making them add up to something bigger, that is the interesting part of this job.
 You'll partner closely with Sales, Engineering, and Product colleagues across the SINGU Group so your portfolio drives revenue and solves real problems across the European FM market. AI is a must-have lever in our industry rather than a talking point: you'll be applying it where it measurably improves how our customers run their estates.
 This is a remote position with periodic travel to London and Kraków – roughly every two to four weeks.
 
 Role Scope 
 
 People Leadership & Team Development: 
 Manage and develop the Product Managers within the product team.

 Own the full management lifecycle: hiring, onboarding, mentorship, feedback, coaching, performance evaluations, promotions, and exits .

 Foster a high-performing product culture based on customer empathy, data-driven decision-making, and outcome orientation.

 Manage staffing and focus areas across the suite, reallocating product resources where needed to balance discovery workload and meet strategic priorities.

 Lead the team through change – new ways of working, a shifting portfolio, and product consolidation – bringing people with you rather than around them.

 
 Product Discovery & Strategy: 
 Define and maintain product roadmaps aligned with business objectives, customer needs, and market trends.

 Decide where to invest and where to hold : set a clear, defensible position on which initiatives scale and communicate it across the business.

 Build strong alignment with the Sales team to ensure product discovery and roadmap priorities actively unblock deals and support revenue growth.

 Identify and resolve ambiguities, dependencies, and competing priorities that impact discovery quality and speed.

 
 Product Management Best Practices & Standards: 
 Promote modern product practices, including continuous discovery, outcome-based roadmapping, and hypothesis-driven development .

 Ensure product teams consistently validate assumptions through user research, experimentation, and data analysis .

 Drive improvements in requirements quality, stakeholder communication, prioritization frameworks, and release planning.

 Cooperate with the Chief Architect and Engineering Managers to ensure product decisions account for technical feasibility and platform constraints.

 Drive the adoption of AI-powered tools and analytics to improve product insights, customer understanding, and decision-making quality.

 
 Collaboration & Cross-Company Coordination: 
 Coordinate with commercial and customer-facing teams to align product strategy with go-to-market plans and revenue goals for the portfolio.

About Welo Global 

 Welo Global is a leader in multilingual AI, technology, and content solutions serving over 2,000 clients in 300 languages. You will be the main point of contact for the client’s Language Manager on quality discussions, arbitration, and escalations, and you will drive consistency, quality governance, and continuous improvement across UI, marketing, product, informational, legal, and support content.

 What You Will Do 

 -Analyse requirements: Review every style guide and glossary update, assess which quality categories and content types it affects, and record the changes. Track what the client’s Language Manager actually corrects and says in calibration and quality calls, not only what is written down.

 -Maintain alignment with the client: Treat Language Manager decisions as the standard, raise concerns with evidence at the right forum, and aim for fewer surprises over time. 

 What You Will Own 

 -The locale’s review service score, including RQE audit and alignment performance
-The community’s shared understanding of quality

-The working relationship with the client’s Language Manager, including clarifications, escalations, and expectation tracking

- Client and stakeholder management: Direct experience as the primary point of contact for client Language Managers, managing formal arbitration or escalation processes, and facilitating conflict resolution 
- Quality audit frameworks: Deep, practical experience with localization evaluation frameworks, including RQE, LQE, error rubrics, and severity mapping 
- Style guide and expectation analysis: Ability to analyse style guide changes, identify implicit client expectations, and map tolerance by content type (for example, Marketing vs. Legal vs. UI) 
- Meeting facilitation: Hands-on experience with one-to-one coaching, shadowing sessions, alignment roundtables, and structured monthly quality reporting 
- Analytical approach: Skill in tracking error concentrations, severity drift, and alignment scores, and in converting justification patterns into style guide improvements 
- Language: Native-level German (Switzerland) and professional-level English
- Preferred: Prior e xperience supporting major technology localization programs and working with calibration or alignment tools
